rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~88% 25bp / ~12% 50bp (CME FedWatch); ECB Dec ~88%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~32–36%; US 2Y ~4.85%
rows.read: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly joined the officials saying more rate rises are likely, and a December Fed hike is close to certain. Europe, Britain and Japan are also expected to hike, but US rates are rising faster, so the gap keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Euro-area Q3 GDP +0.4% q/q (unrevised), employment flat; UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q; US retail sales Tue 7:30 AM CT
rows.read: Euro-area growth was confirmed at a decent pace for the summer quarter, but it did not lift the euro. The US economy still looks firmer than Australia, Canada or New Zealand, which keeps the dollar ahead of those currencies. US retail sales on Tuesday are the next check.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US PPI Oct +0.3% m/m (fcst +0.4%), +6.5% y/y; core +0.3% m/m in line; Japan wholesale prices +7.1% y/y
rows.read: US wholesale prices cooled a touch in October but still run far above what the Fed wants, so the pressure to hike stays. That keeps supporting the dollar. In Japan, a weak yen is pushing wholesale prices up fast.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: USD/CHF ~0.837; AUD/USD ~0.678; NZD/USD ~0.553; CENTCOM: two IRGC drones shot down, radar-hit claim rejected
rows.read: Iran's claims of strikes in the Gulf were denied or unconfirmed, so markets stayed calm and the safe-haven franc and yen got no lift. The Aussie and kiwi, which track the market mood, ended the week near their lows.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$96.1, WTI ~$88.9; Brent about −2.5% on the week; gold ~$3,887
rows.read: Oil held near Thursday's jump, but the International Energy Agency says the market is back in surplus, which caps prices. Dearer oil helps the Canadian dollar and hurts energy buyers like Japan and the euro area. Gold stayed well below $4,000, taking some support from the Aussie.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; 4-week change NZD −22K, EUR −34K contracts; Nov 10 report not yet posted at 3:00 PM CT
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, and this week's moves went their way. Their large bet on the yen keeps losing money as it weakens. The newest weekly report from US regulators had not been published by the close.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.13%, largest weekly sell-off in over 18 months
rows.read: Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs above 5%, and this was their biggest weekly rise in more than a year and a half. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but a growing deficit is a worry if buyers start asking for more.
